chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Aba Ja'far عليه السلام saying:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would not perform any salat (prayer) during the daytime until the sun declined. When it had declined by about half a finger, he performed eight rak'ahs. When the shadow reached one cubit, he performed the zuhr prayer; then after zuhr he performed two rak'ahs, and before the time of 'asr he would perform two rak'ahs. When the shadow reached two cubits, he performed the 'asr prayer. He performed the maghrib prayer when the sun set, and when the twilight disappeared, the time of the 'isha' prayer began. The end of the time of maghrib is the return of the twilight; when the twilight returned, the time of 'isha' began. The end of the time of 'isha' is one-third of the night. He would not perform salat after 'isha' until the middle of the night; then he would perform thirteen rak'ahs, including al-witr and including the two rak'ahs of fajr before the morning prayer. When dawn rose and became bright, he performed the morning prayer.

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, marking the beginning of the morning prayer time
key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: the returning shadow used to determine prayer times
key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: the odd-numbered concluding prayer of the night vigil
key_terms.تَزُولَ: to decline from the zenith, referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: one cubit, a measure of shadow length

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the times of maghrib and 'isha' prayers and the Prophet’s daily prayer routine?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the prayer schedule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم across the day and night, including supererogatory prayers and the timings of the obligatory salat. It is significant for understanding the beginnings and limits of the times of maghrib and 'isha', as well as the Prophet’s regular worship practice.
